name: Villa de Leyva
tagline: Colonial town with one of the largest plazas in the Americas
summary: Villa de Leyva is a whitewashed colonial town in the dry hills of Boyacá with an enormous cobbled plaza. See giant fossils at the El Fósil museum, the ancient El Infiernito observatory, the strange clay Casa Terracota, and hike to the Pozos Azules pools.
seasonNote: Mild and dry; festivals in August (kites) and December (lights).
arrival: About 4 hours by bus from Bogotá via Tunja.
cashTip: Carry pesos for small places and transport; cards work in hotels. A 10 percent service is often suggested on the bill.
foodTip: Ajiaco, cuchuco soup and local wines from Boyacá.
